radiology_report:
Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede)
Department of Radiology
Date: 05 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation of known prostate cancer. PSA 68.0 ng/mL. Prior biopsy Gleason 4+3 ISUP GG3.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume is 58.83 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a large, irregular, hypointense lesion in the right peripheral zone, measuring approximately 32 mm in craniocaudal dimension. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows markedly restricted diffusion in this region. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate early and intense enhancement of the lesion. There is clear evidence of extracapsular extension, with tumour tissue breaching the prostatic capsule laterally and abutting the neurovascular bundle. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or osseous metastases are identified.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone with extracapsular extension. Clinical T stage cT3. PSA density 1.156 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.8985173.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (oldest):
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals acinar adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 4+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 3. Perineural invasion is present. The tumour is located in the right side of the gland. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified.

Biopsy timepoint 2 (latest):
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals acinar adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 4+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 3. Perineural invasion is present. The tumour is located in the right side of the gland. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified.

The histological grade has remained stable across the two biopsy timepoints.
